title: Counting Stored Days on the Storage Lot — Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Repossessions
content:
For a repossessed vehicle under a Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Installment Sale Contract, the stored days on a storage charge through a statement date follow where the vehicle has been held. The lot-intake date is the date of the most recent condition report on the contract, the first one listed where two share a date.

| Recovery and lot intake | Stored days |
|---|---|
| Involuntary recovery whose lot-intake date is after the repossession date | from the day after the lot-intake date through the statement date — the agency held the vehicle until then and billed that holding on its transport charge |
| Voluntary surrender | from the repossession date through the statement date, both included — the surrender day itself counts |
| Any other case, including a contract with no condition report on record and an involuntary recovery whose most recent report is dated on or before the repossession date | from the day after the repossession date through the statement date |

### Hypothetical counts (statement date on the 20th)

| Records | Stored days |
|---|---|
| Involuntary, repossessed on the 5th, most recent condition report on the 8th | the 9th through the 20th: 12 |
| Involuntary, repossessed on the 5th, condition report on the 5th | the 6th through the 20th: 15 |
| Voluntary surrender on the 5th | the 5th through the 20th: 16 |
| Involuntary, repossessed on the 5th, no condition report | the 6th through the 20th: 15 |

### Lot days for the charge billed when the vehicle leaves the lot

For the storage billed when the vehicle leaves the lot, storage is billed only for days the vehicle is on the storage lot, and each such day only once. The lot days of an involuntary recovery whose most recent condition report is dated after the repossession date run from the day after that lot-intake date, the nights before it being the agency's holding, billed on its transport charge and never as storage; the lot days of a voluntary surrender run from the repossession date itself; any other lot days run from the day after the repossession date. A lot day up to and including the latest statement date on which a storage charge was billed is billed by that charge, whatever the charge came to, and a lot day collected in a redemption figure or a reinstatement amount or counted into a deficiency quote is not billed again.
